nodes.name: Cathodic electrodeposition of Ni(OH)₂ films
nodes.procedure: Electrocatalytic Ni(OH)₂ films were cathodically deposited on Ti foil using a two-electrode configuration following previous guidelines. Films were deposited galvanostatically at -1 mA cm⁻² (thickness: ~110 nm for most experiments, ~550 nm for ICP-MS samples).

nodes.name: Cathodic electrodeposition of NiCo(OH)₂ films
nodes.procedure: NiCo(OH)₂ films with varying Co content were deposited on Ti foil and gold interdigitated array (IDA) electrodes at -1 mA cm⁻². Deposition times were optimized to ensure consistent film thicknesses (~110 nm) and prevent detachment. Film thickness was measured via non-contact profilometry.

nodes.name: Fe-doping of Ni mesh
nodes.procedure: Fe-doped Ni mesh anodes were prepared by conditioning a Ni gauze strip in KOH electrolyte spiked with Fe (1 mM) via CV cycling.
nodes.source_text: Fe-doped Ni mesh anodes were prepared by conditioning a Ni gauze strip in KOH electrolyte spiked with Fe (1 mM).

nodes.description: Electrode discharge during simulated shutdown (O₂ electrode)
nodes.source_text: OCP decay profiles following abruptly interrupting galvanostatic polarization at 25 mA cm⁻² in 0.1 M KOH electrolyte. Electrodes consist of Ni(OH)₂ films deposited on Ti foil substrates.

Steady-state operation led to a gradual increase in cell and electrode potentials, with minimal or negligible variation in the HFR. Only Ni(OH)₂/TF exhibits an initial stabilization phase, where the electrode potential increases at 46.9 mV h⁻¹ before slowing to 4.7 mV h⁻¹.

nodes.description: Accelerated catalyst degradation with reverse current (all catalysts tested)

degradation_pattern.value: initial rise in overpotential, followed by sharp increase of several hundred mV/h

redox_feature.value: progressive disappearance of M²⁺/³⁺ redox feature

nodes.source_text: To study the role of reverse currents, we then replaced the OCP step with a reverse current of -5 mA cm⁻²... The electrodes deteriorated rapidly under reverse currents, with degradation rates varying with film composition.

nodes.description: In situ SERS phase transformation during deep discharge
nodes.source_text: The electrode potential drops rapidly following the galvanostatic step, exhibiting the Ni²⁺/³⁺ redox transition before stabilizing after 380 s at ∼0.8 V vs RHE. Raman spectra collected at regular intervals consistently show oxyhydroxide bands throughout this period.

nodes.description: Zero-gap electrolyzer variable operation with Ni mesh electrodes
nodes.source_text: Electrodes were operated at steady state at 120 mA cm⁻² followed by discharge at a constant reverse current of -0.25 mA cm⁻² cm⁻²... The total cell potential increases at a rate of ∼0.2 mV h⁻¹

nodes.source_text: CP at 1.35 mA cm⁻², followed by a reverse step at -1.35 mA cm⁻². Concomitantly, Ni, Co, Fe, and Ti concentrations in the KOH electrolyte exiting the flow cell were measured.

nodes.description: ToF-SIMS composition analysis after variable operation
nodes.source_text: After variable operation, the depth distribution ranges decrease significantly... indicating substantial thinning of the catalytic film (i.e., from ∼110 to ∼40 nm). The NiCo(OH)₂/TF electrode lost 62.6% of Ni and 11.5% of Co

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy reveals hydroxide-to-oxyhydroxide phase transition in Ni(OH)₂ with characteristic bands shifting from 458, 495, 694 cm⁻¹ (hydroxide) to 477, 558 cm⁻¹ (oxyhydroxide).
nodes.evidence_snippet: we observe the characteristic Raman bands of the hydroxide phase at 458, 495, and 694 cm⁻¹ shift to those of oxyhydroxide at 477 and 558 cm⁻¹ at potentials positive of the Ni²⁺/³⁺ redox peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: Depth profiles show pristine NiCo(OH)₂ film thickness ~110 nm (Ni, Co, O fragments), reducing to ~40 nm after variable operation with Ti emerging at ~20 nm depth.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Secondary ion fragments containing Ni, Co, and O are primarily distributed within the top ~110 nm of the pristine NiCo(OH)₂/TF electrode... After variable operation... Ti⁻ fragment now emerges at just ~20 nm from the electrode surface, indicating substantial thinning... from ~110 to ~40 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Depth profiles show pristine NiFe(OH)₂ film thickness ~160 nm, reducing to ~130 nm after variable operation testing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the NiFe(OH)₂/TF electrode undergoes thinning of the catalytic film, decreasing from ~160 to ~130 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ ICP-MS shows NiCo(OH)₂/TF electrode lost 62.6% of Ni and 11.5% of Co, while NiFe(OH)₂/TF lost 98.2% of Ni and 74.7% of Fe after variable operation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S56 (ESI†), the NiCo(OH)₂/TF electrode lost 62.6% of Ni and 11.5% of Co, while the NiFe(OH)₂/TF electrode lost 98.2% of Ni and 74.7% of Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ measurements on IDA electrodes show NiCo(OH)₂ films with 13 mol% Co have effective conductivity ~4 orders of magnitude higher than pure Ni above 0.4 V vs. Hg/HgO, plateauing above 0.54 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: films with 13 mol% Co exhibit an effective conductivity nearly four orders of magnitude higher than pure Ni films above 0.4 V vs. Hg/HgO. Note that the conductivity plateaus above 0.54 V vs. Hg/HgO for all NiCo(OH)₂ films.

nodes.characterization_summary: Online ICP-MS during variable operation shows Co stabilizes at 30.5 ng mL⁻¹ cm⁻² (r_ds=1.01 ng s⁻¹ cm⁻²) with reoxidation spikes; Ni decreases 30→20 ng mL⁻¹ cm⁻²; Ti doubles during reverse current.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co concentration... stabilizing at ~30.5 ng mL⁻¹ cm⁻² (equivalent to a dissolution rate, r_ds, of 1.01 ng s⁻¹ cm⁻²). Sharp Co concentration spikes consistently appear upon reoxidation... Ni concentration steadily decreases from ~30 to ~20 ng mL⁻¹ cm⁻²... concentration of Ti rises under reverse currents to nearly twice its baseline value.

nodes.characterization_summary: Postmortem XPS reveals higher Ni(OH)₂ content at H₂ electrode compared to O₂ electrode; Fe-doped Ni mesh shows significant Fe content decrease after cycling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Postmortem X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis reveals a higher Ni(OH)₂ content at the H₂ electrode compared to the O₂ electrode... ex situ XPS reveals a significant decrease in Fe content in the Fe-doped Ni mesh electrode after cycling.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows HFR stable at 11-14 Ω cm² across Ni, Co, NiCo, NiFe hydroxide electrodes; R_ct increases drastically during reverse current degradation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HFR remains stable within the 11-14 Ω cm² range across all electrodes. Nyquist plots initially display two semicircles... Eventually, a single semicircle develops with a drastic rise in the R_ct.

nodes.characterization_summary: Corrosion potentials follow Ni(OH)₂ (767.3 mV) < NiFe(OH)₂ < NiCo(OH)₂ trend; increases with KOH concentration (767.3→665 mV, 0.1→7 M); decreases with temperature (767.3→635 mV, 20→50°C).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt and Ni foil electrodes exhibit corrosion potentials of 825 and 840 mV... Ni(OH)₂ O₂ electrode (767.3 mV)... Corrosion potentials follow the trend Ni(OH)₂ < NiFe(OH)₂ < NiCo(OH)₂... Increasing the KOH... from 767.3 to 665 mV... raising the temperature... lowers it to 635 mV.
